decision.summary: 30 of 34 findings are evidence-backed; 4 were insufficient and recorded for follow-up.

findings.statement: Noon is an e‑commerce and digital services company operating in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.
Noon connects consumers with retailers and brands through online shopping, grocery delivery, and logistics services.
Strategic Goal: Increase active customers by 20% and reduce delivery times by 10% across current markets by the end of 2026.
Ticket OPS‑1042 (Reduce Late Deliveries) is high priority, in progress, and cites delivery delays in selected Egyptian cities with a need to investigate warehouse bottlenecks and courier allocation.
Ticket MKT‑2081 (Improve Repeat Purchases) is high priority, open, and targets a 15% increase in repeat purchases by year‑end and a 15% reduction in late deliveries within eight weeks.

Mock pricing sheet (hypothetical) lists average order values of EGP 4,500 (Electronics), EGP 1,200 (Fashion), and EGP 2,000 (Home & Kitchen) with average discounts of 10%, 15%, and 8% and delivery fees of EGP 60, 45, and 50 respectively.
Mock performance snapshot (hypothetical) shows an on‑time delivery rate of 88% and a repeat purchase rate of 34%.

Key strategic risks identified include competitors increasing discounts and promotional spending, delivery costs rising faster than order volume, and customer churn caused by inconsistent delivery experiences.
The global B2B ecommerce market will grow at a 14.5% compound annual growth rate through 2026.
The global B2B ecommerce market is valued at USD $36 trillion by 2026.
APAC will comprise 80% of B2B market share by 2026.
Digital wallets accounted for 20% of online spending in MENA in 2023.
Mobile commerce is expected to represent 70% of online transaction value by 2025.
Over half of internet users in Saudi Arabia shopped online weekly in 2023.
Mobile commerce (m-commerce) has fundamentally reshaped the retail landscape.
European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a key data protection framework.
Indonesia's Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP) is referenced as a national data protection law.
Major data breaches occurred between 2018 and 2024.

Amazon does not charge a monthly subscription fee for third‑party sellers in the UAE and Saudi Arabia as a limited‑time offer, and applies referral fees of 8 % on items with a total sales price of $10.00 or less and 15 % on items priced above $10.00.

Amazon provides the Amazon Pay payment gateway in the MENA region, enabling online merchants in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar, Kuwait and Oman to accept local payments at checkout.

Jarir.com: Jarir positions its online shopping platform as the market leader in the Middle East for consumer IT products, electronics, office supplies and books, emphasizing service quality leadership and affordable, superior‑quality products across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt.

Jarir.com: Jarir offers a Jarir Discount Card that provides a 10% instant discount on most school and office supplies, arts & crafts, books and computer bags, and runs a rewards program (Woow Loyalty) where points or vouchers can be redeemed for purchases; no subscription tiers are mentioned.

Jarir.com: Jarir’s delivery options include in‑store showroom pickup with orders ready within one hour, a services centre in each showroom offering product installation, and a return/exchange process that can be completed at any showroom.
Jumia charges sellers a commission based on the product category; for example, a 5 % commission is applied to a 1,000 LE item in category X, resulting in a 50 LE fee to Jumia.

Jumia offers consumer price reductions through discount vouchers and promotional codes, promoting low prices during its "amazing discounts and offers" campaigns and providing discount codes for categories such as home furniture and groceries.

Offering and localisation for those markets: compared with noon, Amazon is comparable. Amazon offers a marketplace with Amazon Pay, local‑language support and same‑day delivery options, delivering a comparable but globally‑focused catalog.
